description: A sepia oil painting of a baseball player in a cap and light jersey, sliding feet-first into a base in a cloud of dust, with the number 42 clearly painted on his back. A fielder in a cap and glove lunges in from the right. Behind them a blurred crowd sits under a roofed grandstand. The painting runs edge to edge with no frame, and a small sparkle logo sits in the bottom right corner. Nothing gory or nude.
reason: Shows a 20th-century baseball slide into a base, but the card is Japanese kana developing around 900. Baseball uniforms, gloves and a stadium crowd are far out of era. The number 42 is clearly painted on the jersey, which is a number in the image. Repaint as early Japanese court scholars or calligraphers writing flowing kana script, with no text visible.
